The constraint we start with

What slows financial services teams down.

We begin with the moments where people wait, repeat work, or lose context. Then we automate the predictable part and keep judgment with the right person.

01

Files stall on documents and KYC

Loan applications, insurance proposals and onboarding files wait on missing pages, blurred scans, name mismatches and Video KYC slots. Teams chase the same items by phone and personal WhatsApp, and good customers drift to a faster lender, insurer or app.

02

Customers cannot see where they stand

Borrowers, policyholders and investors call branches, DSAs, agents and advisers to ask for status because nothing tells them. Every unanswered call erodes trust, and some applicants quietly drop off.

03

Every message is regulated

RBI, IRDAI, SEBI and TRAI set rules on what can be said, when and by whom: Key Fact Statements, recovery contact hours, advertisement approval, return claims and calling-number series. WhatsApp also restricts some financial uses. Automation has to be built inside those lines from the start.

04

Decisions must stay with accountable people

Credit, underwriting, claims, suitability and fraud decisions need a named person and a recorded reason. Tools that blur that line create regulatory, conduct and reputational risk, however efficient they look.

05

EMIs, renewals and SIPs slip quietly

Bounced mandates, lapsed policies and missed SIP installments surface days or weeks later in separate reports, when recovery is harder and the relationship has already suffered.

06

The picture is spread across many systems

LOS, LMS, insurer portals, RTA feeds, gateways, dispute portals and dialers each hold part of the story, so management reports are assembled by hand and rarely reconcile.

The perfect automation

Consent-first application, KYC and status tracker

One connected flow from application to a decision-ready file. Applicants share documents through a secure page or DigiLocker where the regulated entity uses it, KYC steps are tracked, missing items are chased automatically, and every milestone reaches the customer in plain language. Credit officers and underwriters receive complete files and make every decision themselves.

  1. 01

    Capture the application with purpose-bound consent

    Applications from the website, app, branch, DSA or agent reach the LOS or broker system through its API or a scheduled export, with source, product and the consent recorded at each step. Every consent states its purpose, and the applicant can review or withdraw it.

    NNext.jsSSupabasenn8n
  2. 02

    Send the checklist and collect documents securely

    A checklist built from product rules and applicant type goes out by approved WhatsApp utility template or DLT SMS, linking to a page on the lender's or broker's own domain. Documents are uploaded there or fetched from DigiLocker or CKYC where the regulated entity uses those routes, never sent in chat.

    WBWhatsApp Business PlatformNNext.jsSSupabase
  3. 03

    Check completeness and track KYC

    AI on an approved model deployment, hosted in India where required, classifies each document and flags blur, expiry, missing pages and name mismatches for an operations officer to confirm. KYC status is tracked across CKYC download, Video KYC run by the regulated entity's trained officials and any further checks.

    OOpenAInn8nRRetool
  4. 04

    Hand a decision-ready file to credit or underwriting

    Complete files move to the credit or underwriting queue with an extracted summary and open questions. People make and record the decision in the LOS or with the insurer; the tracker only moves the file and never scores, prices or limits.

    RRetoolSSupabase
  5. 05

    Keep the customer informed at every milestone

    Customers hear when the file is received, what is pending, when it is under review, and whether it is approved or declined with the main reasons. Before a borrower signs, the tracker confirms the KFS reached them, and for digital loans it records the cooling-off window the lender's board has set.

    WBWhatsApp Business PlatformRResendnn8n
  6. 06

    One operating view

    A dashboard shows files by stage, age and missing item, KYC exceptions, turnaround by product, branch, DSA and agent, and the steps where applicants drop off.

    MPMicrosoft Power BISSupabase

Human checkpoint

Operations officers verify documents and resolve every KYC exception, and the regulated entity's trained officials conduct Video KYC. Credit officers, underwriters or the insurer decide every application and record the reasons. The tracker never approves, declines, prices or sets limits.

What changes

  • Fewer files stuck on missing or unreadable documents, so credit and underwriting teams spend their time assessing
  • Customers who know where their application stands, and fewer status calls to branches, DSAs and agents
  • A consent, KYC and communication trail that is ready for audit because it is built into the process
  • Turnaround and drop-off visible by product, branch and channel, so managers fix bottlenecks early

Automation playbook

Start where the work repeats.

A selection from the playbook. Each blueprint shows the trigger, steps, tools, human checkpoint, data handling, deliverables, and measures.

Discover and inquire · 3–5 weeks

Inquiry desk with indicative eligibility

Capture loan inquiries from ads, aggregators, the website, WhatsApp and DSAs, ask only what indicative eligibility needs, check it against the lender's published criteria, and route likely applicants to the right owner. It guides; it never decides.

View the blueprint ↗Discover and inquire · 2–4 weeks

Compliance-approved content library and distribution

Draft educational posts, newsletters and WhatsApp updates from approved source material, route each one to the compliance officer, and let advisers and agents share only approved, versioned items that carry the required disclosures.

View the blueprint ↗Apply, verify and decide · 6–10 weeks

Application, KYC and status tracker

Generate the right checklist for each application or proposal, collect documents through a secure page or DigiLocker, track KYC steps, chase what is missing, and keep the customer updated until a person makes the decision.

View the blueprint ↗Apply, verify and decide · 3–5 weeks

Client onboarding and risk-profiling workflow

Take a new advisory client from the first call to a signed agreement, KYC confirmed with a KRA, and a risk profile the client has reviewed and consented to, with every record kept together for the retention period.

View the blueprint ↗Apply, verify and decide · 3–5 weeks

Onboarding drop-off recovery for apps

Detect where users stall in sign-up, such as KYC, bank linking or mandate setup, identify the likely reason, and send one helpful, consented nudge or route the user to support instead of sending blanket reminders.

View the blueprint ↗Apply, verify and decide · 6–9 weeks

Merchant onboarding and due diligence queue

Collect merchant documents, run checks on PAN, GSTIN, bank account and website, assign a risk tier, and give onboarding officers one queue, so no merchant goes live before due diligence is complete and approved.

How we work

A clear delivery rhythm, from discovery to daily operation.

Five phases with named deliverables, client inputs, and review points. Most teams start with a focused pilot.

  1. 01 · 1–2 weeksDiscover

    We sit with credit operations, collections, service, claims, advisory or risk teams to map how customers actually apply, pay, claim and complain, and which systems hold the data. We confirm what the LOS, LMS, insurer portals, RTA feeds and gateways allow through APIs or exports, review the current consent and channel setup, and choose the first journey.

  2. 02 · 1–2 weeksDesign

    We design flows, customer pages, checklists, routing rules, response targets and approval points, and write WhatsApp, DLT SMS and email templates. Consent wording, KYC handling, data localization, retention and the exact point where each person decides are designed with the client's compliance officer before anything is built.

  3. 03 · 2–6 weeksBuild

    We build workflows in n8n or code, secure customer pages and staff consoles, retrieval-based assistants over approved documents, and the connections to client systems. Everything runs in a staging setup with masked data, hosted in India wherever the data or the regulator requires it.

  4. 04 · 1–2 weeksValidate & launch

    Teams test real scenarios: a blurred PAN card, a bounced mandate, a motor claim reported at night, a stale risk profile, a chargeback close to its deadline. We evaluate AI answers against approved documents, confirm contact windows and consent checks, launch on one product, branch or team first, and train every shift.

  5. 05 · Ongoing, reviewed monthlyOperate & improve

    We monitor workflow health, deadlines, contact-rule checks and AI quality, fix failures, and review results with the client each month. Regulatory changes, such as RBI's recovery amendments that apply from January 2027 or SEBI's new advertisement code, are reviewed with the compliance officer and reflected in rules and templates.

Suggested first pilot

One product, one journey, four to six weeks

We start where volume and pain are highest. For a lender that is usually checklists, secure uploads and status updates for one product, before the full KYC tracker. For a broker it is motor and health renewals, for an advisory firm onboarding and risk profiling, and for a fintech onboarding drop-off recovery or a dispute queue for one dispute source. A baseline taken in the first week makes the comparison honest.

  • One product or team and one customer journey
  • Approved WhatsApp and DLT SMS templates and a secure customer page
  • Integration with the LOS, broker system, MF back office or gateway in read and limited write mode
  • A staff console for the queue, with escalation to a named owner
  • Weekly check-ins and a go or no-go review at the end of the pilot

Measures

Know whether it is working.

Proposed measures, agreed with your team before launch, with a source, owner, and review cadence.

First response time to inquiries

Median elapsed time from a new inquiry on any connected channel to the first meaningful reply by the system or a person, by channel, product and hour of day.

Files complete at first submission

Applications, proposals or merchant files with every required document and KYC step complete when first sent for decision, divided by all files sent for decision in the period.

Application turnaround time

Median elapsed time from a complete application to a recorded decision, and from decision to disbursal, issuance or activation, by product and channel.

Onboarding drop-off by step

Share of applicants who start but do not finish each onboarding step, such as document upload, Video KYC, bank verification or mandate setup, by channel and cohort.
